findings.explanation: The description names '-7d' as the alert condition, but in the SPL it is only the search window (earliest=-7d). The SPL has no threshold, so every matching event row would alert. The description and SPL describe different detections.
findings.suggested_fix: State the real alert condition (for example any camera with one or more tamper events in the window, or a count threshold the author chooses) and make the description, controlTest and SPL agree on it.

findings.explanation: The SPL matches tamper|vandal|cover|defocus on event_type. It never looks at vibration data or access logs, and the implementation gives no step for deduplication or correlation. The steps are too thin to follow and describe a different detection.
findings.quote: (2) Deduplicate vibration spikes. (3) Correlate with access logs.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the steps around what the SPL does: how the ISAPI tamper or video-tampering events reach HEC, which field carries the event type, and how to throttle repeated events per camera. Only keep vibration or access-log correlation if the SPL implements it.

findings.explanation: The SPL uses earliest=-7d, so the scheduling advice contradicts it. The text also describes joins and lookups that the SPL does not contain, and the validation step compares event counts to a vendor 'inventory count', which does not apply to tamper events.
findings.suggested_fix: Align the schedule window with the SPL and drop the generic joins/lookups and inventory-count text. Validate instead by triggering a lens-cover or tamper event on a test camera and confirming it arrives.

findings.explanation: This sourcetype does not appear in the integration guide or the sibling use cases, and no add-on is shown that produces it. The event_type values the SPL matches ('tamper', 'vandal', 'cover', 'defocus') are also not Hikvision ISAPI event-type names that I can confirm; Hikvision names video tampering events differently, such as shelteralarm.
findings.suggested_fix: Check Hikvision's ISAPI alarm/event notification documentation for the real event type names and payload format. Document how the custom sourcetype is defined, or use a sourcetype from the guide.

findings.explanation: A Universal Forwarder is not a Splunkbase app, and modular inputs generally run on a full Splunk instance or heavy forwarder. The same sentence is reused across the sibling UCs, so it looks like boilerplate. The app field's Splunkbase ID is flagged separately.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: Check what Splunkbase 617 is, and name the actual collection path (HEC endpoint, heavy forwarder modular input or script) that the implementation text uses.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified, but the sourcetype, event types and fields are unconfirmed and the text is template residue. Nothing shows SME sign-off, and the reviewer is a generic 'catalog-team'.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the status to draft until a named SME has validated the data source and detection against real Hikvision ISAPI events.

findings.explanation: The Splunk Search Reference URL contains an apostrophe. The repository's own reference uses 'WhatsInThisManual', so this link is probably broken. The Hikvision link is a generic SDK download page rather than ISAPI event documentation.
findings.suggested_fix: Use https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/Splunk/latest/SearchReference/WhatsInThisManual and link the ISAPI alarm/event documentation.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: The SPL has no threshold or time grain, so any single matching event in 7 days produces a row. It also relies on an event_type field whose extraction is not documented, and the match for 'cover' is broad.

summary: The description reads as title words strung together, and it states an 'alert when -7d' condition that the SPL does not implement. The implementation text mentions vibration and access-log correlation that the detection never touches, and the sourcetype and event_type values are unverified.
